title: Waterschap Limburg answers on timestamps, zeros, rating history and thresholds
retrieval_text: Waterschap Limburg says timestamps use fixed GMT+1 all year without daylight saving. Zero means exactly 0.000 m3/s; blanks mean unavailable. Delivered discharge uses the rating relation applicable to each period and may be retrospectively corrected. Only current Fase thresholds are retained. Historical thresholds, reference datum history and sensor history are unavailable. Cottessen flume capacity is about 26 m3/s and the Geul inundates above it.

title: Waterschap Limburg July 2021 station-function report
retrieval_text: July 2021 station report: Cottessen water level continued but discharge exceeded the 27.5 m3/s rating range and was disturbed by inundation and deposits. Rimburg stage reached 86.427 m NAP, above the documented 86.027 m rating limit. Gulp Azijnfabriek rating documentation reports poor accuracy and calibration only to about 3 m3/s. Molentak is an automatically controlled branch.

title: Audited Waterschap source semantics and July 2021 implications
retrieval_text: The audit distinguishes blanks from true zero, applies fixed UTC+1, and records per-station July 2021 quality limits. Cottessen and Rimburg peak discharge are outside supported rating domains. Gulp high flow is uncertain. Molentak is excluded from the natural-tributary cohort because an automatic weir controls the branch.

title: Current Waterschap H1 H2 H3 discharge thresholds
retrieval_text: Current thresholds in m3/s. H1 increased vigilance, H2 imminent flood risk, H3 flooding. Cottessen 10.Q.29: 10, 20, 27.5. Rimburg 18.Q.45: 25, 32, 40. Eyserbeek Eys 11.Q.32: 5.25, 6.2, 7.5. These are current values and not a historical series.

title: Audited Waterschap rating-era table
retrieval_text: Rating-era table gives validity periods and discharge domains. Cottessen 10.Q.29 has documented domain 0.5 to 27.5 m3/s. Rimburg 18.Q.45 has a documented July 2021-era maximum of 44.627 m3/s, while the separate stage-domain evidence limits interpretation of the peak.

title: Checked Dutch high-water onset table
retrieval_text: Checked event table contains exact adjacent-hour p99 crossings, rating era, discharge domain, gap and measurement-concern flags, provider status, storm ID and whether rainfall and weather histories are complete. It supports event-specific calculations but does not provide official warning decisions.

title: Six-gauge Dutch tributary register
retrieval_text: Gauge identities: 11.Q.32 Eyserbeek, 10.Q.29 Geul at Cottessen, 13.Q.34 Gulp, 15.Q.41 Voer, 18.Q.45 Worm at Rimburg and 6.Q.18 Geleenbeek. The table records July 2021 status and verified source semantics.

title: Four LANUK station packages
retrieval_text: LANUK packages cover Herzogenrath 1, Herzogenrath 2, Honsdorf and Randerath with 15-minute stage/discharge and rating files. Herzogenrath 1 and Randerath are nested Wurm stations. Herzogenrath 2 is on Broicher Bach. Honsdorf is on Beeckflies.

title: LANUK Honsdorf replacement stage delivery
retrieval_text: Honsdorf is on Beeckflies. Replacement stage data are 15-minute means on a complete fixed grid. The current gauge zero is 54.368 m NHN2016, but this does not establish historical datum or sensor stability. Remaining reconstruction and provisional-rating questions were still pending.

title: Honsdorf stage receipt and audit
retrieval_text: The replacement Honsdorf stage export has 534,721 quarter-hour rows and 12 blanks. July 2021 stage and discharge maxima share the source timestamp 2021-07-14 13:15. That crosswalk does not validate peak discharge or the stage-discharge relation. The current gauge zero cannot be applied to historical records without datum-history evidence.

title: RWS Maas observation-quality audit
retrieval_text: RWS quality code 25 means interpolation in space and time. Venlo discharge from 12 to 20 July 2021 is almost entirely code 25, so the apparent rise in the permissive series is largely interpolated and is excluded from the strict measured-discharge analysis. Code 00 is the strict controlled observation screen.

title: RWS bulk-observation attribute guide
retrieval_text: Official RWS bulk-observation guidance defines quality and processing attributes. The held audit uses it to distinguish controlled code 00 from code 25 interpolation in space and time.

title: Comparison of northwestern European flood early-warning systems
retrieval_text: Northwestern European FEWS use different warning levels, codes, roles and translations from forecast to action. Cross-border warning exchange remains difficult even where data exchange is relatively organized. The paper does not make Dutch and German warning categories equivalent.

title: International Meuse flood-risk management plan
retrieval_text: The international Meuse plan documents country-specific institutional roles and flood-risk communication. It supports cross-border agency context but does not replace national station metadata or establish equivalence between warning thresholds.
